content.value_statement: Hybrid cloud design spans platforms, networks, security, data placement, and cost controls. This skill provides structured architecture guidance for public cloud, private cloud, Kubernetes, edge, compliance, and FinOps planning.
actual_capabilities: Compares workload placement options across AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, and edge platforms.
Plans hybrid connectivity using dedicated links, VPNs, SD-WAN, DNS, routing, and traffic optimization patterns.
Guides security and compliance design for identity federation, encryption, monitoring, zero trust, and regulated workloads.
Supports migration, disaster recovery, backup, failover, observability, and business continuity planning.
Applies cost, performance, data gravity, capacity, and FinOps factors to architecture decisions.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not environment-specific validation or deployment guarantees.
It does not include executable scripts, Terraform modules, diagrams, or implementation files.
It references an implementation playbook, but this package only contains SKILL.md.
It depends on accurate user inputs for compliance, latency, budget, and platform constraints.

use_cases.title: Plan regulated hybrid platforms
use_cases.description: Design workload placement, identity, encryption, network segmentation, and recovery patterns for regulated AWS, Azure, GCP, and private cloud estates.

use_cases.title: Modernize legacy infrastructure
use_cases.description: Create phased migration plans that combine on-premises systems, OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, and public cloud services.

use_cases.title: Optimize multi-cloud spend
use_cases.description: Evaluate right-sizing, reserved capacity, workload placement, cost allocation, monitoring, and return on investment across hybrid environments.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Hybrid Cloud Goal
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery for a new initiative.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me clarify a hybrid cloud architecture goal. Ask for the business outcome, current platforms, workloads, compliance needs, latency needs, budget limits, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Workload Placement Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning across cloud and private platforms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare placement options for these workloads across AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, VMware, and Kubernetes. Consider cost, latency, compliance, data gravity, resiliency, and operational complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Design Hybrid Connectivity and Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hybrid connectivity and security model for multiple clouds and on-premises systems. Include routing, DNS, VPN or dedicated links, identity federation, segmentation, encryption, monitoring, and failover.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Migration and DR Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced transformation planning with recovery requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased migration and disaster recovery roadmap for a hybrid estate. Include assessment, wave planning, rollback, RTO, RPO, backup, failover testing, observability, FinOps, and governance milestones.

output_examples.input: Design a hybrid cloud architecture for a financial services workload with strict compliance requirements.
output_examples.output: A structured architecture brief covering regulated workload placement, private connectivity, identity federation, encryption, monitoring, disaster recovery, compliance controls, and validation questions.

output_examples.input: Plan workload placement for a global manufacturing company with edge sites and central analytics.
output_examples.output: A placement strategy that separates edge processing, regional data aggregation, central analytics, connectivity patterns, latency tradeoffs, and cost optimization steps.

output_examples.input: Optimize costs for workloads spread across public cloud and OpenStack.
output_examples.output: A FinOps review with right-sizing actions, reserved capacity candidates, chargeback guidance, monitoring improvements, and workload moves based on cost and performance.

best_practices: Provide current platforms, workloads, constraints, data classes, compliance requirements, latency targets, and budget limits before asking for architecture guidance.
Ask for tradeoffs between cost, performance, security, compliance, availability, and operational complexity.
Validate recommendations with platform owners, security teams, network teams, and real environment tests before implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for unrelated software, writing, or office productivity tasks.
Do not treat generated guidance as a final production design without validation and expert review.
Do not ask for executable deployment artifacts when the package only provides advisory architecture guidance.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, Red Hat OpenShift, and edge cloud patterns.

faq.question: Can it design secure hybrid connectivity?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide dedicated links, VPNs, DNS, routing, segmentation, zero trust, encryption, and monitoring patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate deployable infrastructure code?
faq.answer: No. It discusses Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Bicep, Heat, Pulumi, and CDK patterns, but it does not include modules.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated environments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan around HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC2, FedRAMP, data sovereignty, identity, encryption, and audit requirements.

faq.question: Can it help with disaster recovery planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports RTO, RPO, backup, recovery, failover, testing, and business continuity planning across clouds and on-premises systems.

faq.question: What information should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide platforms, workload details, constraints, compliance needs, latency targets, budget limits, current risks, and desired outcomes.
